propositions: set_baseline previously stamped baseline_advanced_at unconditionally on every call despite the stamp having no production reader, causing pathological git delta churn in the bindings.json file across consecutive reconciler passes.

Implementing an equality guard that early-returns when the stored baseline equals the inbound baseline, combined with removing the volatile timestamp write, reduces marginal pack cost from 13.84 KiB/version to 2.33 KiB/version (16.8%) while preserving present-null baseline semantics.
Two consecutive reconciler passes over unchanged Jira state must produce byte-identical bindings.json and identical git HEAD to prove the write-when-changed guard prevents spurious commits.
The five mirrored baseline fields must be filtered on write, and a baseline value of None must round-trip as present to maintain the original ADR 0026 contract.
No production code path or test suite may read the clock or write baseline_advanced_at after the change, verified by identifier search and fail-fast unit controls.
